question.text: Rajiv has a total income of Rs. 18,00,000 during FY 2025-26 under the new tax regime. What is his income tax liability before surcharge and cess?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the new regime FY 2025-26 slabs applied on total income of Rs. 18,00,000: Up to 4L = Nil; 4-8L = 4L x 5% = Rs. 20,000; 8-12L = 4L x 10% = Rs. 40,000; 12-16L = 4L x 15% = Rs. 60,000; 16-18L = 2L x 20% = Rs. 40,000. Total tax = 20,000 + 40,000 + 60,000 + 40,000 = Rs. 1,60,000. The Trap: Rs. 2,40,000 is a distractor that results from incorrectly applying 30% only to the income above Rs. 10 lakh and ignoring the lower-slab tax. Rs. 1,70,000 comes from mistakenly applying 25% instead of 20% on the 16-18L slab. Rs. 1,50,000 omits one slab layer. Note: NISM Series X-B workbook (page 314) sets the FY 2025-26 new-regime slabs that produce Rs. 1,60,000 tax on Rs. 18,00,000 of total income.
